title: weekly-sync-serving-runtime-infra-console-agenda-prep-2026-04-20
content:
Weekly sync prep (serving-runtime / infra / console) - 2026-04-20
Owner: Evelyn Park (serving-runtime infra lead)

Purpose:
- Align on high-priority operational risks for the upcoming week (latency, capacity, console regressions).
- Quick status from owners, unblock cross-team dependencies, capture action items.
- Decide go/no-go on canary expansion for kernel selection rollout.

Attendees (TBD)
- Eng: Evelyn Park, Marcus Liu, Sofia Ramirez, Derek O'Neal
- SRE/Infra: Priya Nair, Tomas Jensen
- Console/Product: Maya Singh, Alex Cho
- Invitees for specific deep dives: Jim Park (observability), Lina Gomez (private deploys)

Duration: 30 minutes
Format: 5m Rundown -> 20m focused issues -> 5m action-item review

Agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot (Evelyn, 5m)
   - p50/p95/p99 generation latency (hosted) - recent uptick on p99 for short-context calls (see Confluence note).
   - GPU pool utilization across Dedicated clusters (east-us-1) - burst capacity used 72% last 24h.
   - Console error rates: surge in 500s for model-metadata endpoints after rollout.
   Note: bring exact numbers if possible; if not, call out data gaps.

2) Canary kernel-selection rollout (Marcus, 8m)
   - Current state: Canary v2 rolled to 5% traffic on 3/4 dedicated pools. Observed 1.8% increase in tail latency for long-context Llama-2-variant.
   - Risk assessment: memory fragmentation on RTXA100 hosts; potential impact on throughput.
   - Decision needed: Hold expansion or expand to 15% with extra KPIs and auto-rollback rule.
   - Prep ask: Marcus to surface perf dashboard link and current flamegraphs (JIRA RT-2145).

3) Console regression triage (Sofia, 6m)
   - Symptoms: Intermittent 500s when fetching model manifests; appears correlated with higher request fanout to metadata service.
   - Tentative root cause hypothesis: caching TTL change + bursty metadata reads after model onboarding flows.
   - Quick mitigations: revert TTL change, rate-limit metadata fetcher, add hotspot cache entries for most common models.

4) Autoscaling / burst capacity policy update for Dedicated (Priya/Derek, 6m)
   - Current policy: scale up at 75% p95 utilization with 8m cool-down; observed thrash during diurnal load when burst capacity queued.
   - Proposal: introduce smoothing window (5m moving avg) and allow one immediate burst per hour per pool.
   - Impact: likely reduce failed enqueue events and maintain latency SLOs; need cost estimate from cost-ops.

5) Action-item review + AOB (5m)

Prep notes (personal scratchpad)
- Gather p99 numbers for the last 72h (hosted and dedicated) and include breakdown by model family and seq_len buckets.
- Pull recent incidents related to metadata API (last 14 days) and summarize root causes.
- Quick check on KV cache hit rates for the canary models - Marcus to share.
- Confirm SRE availability for immediate rollback if canary expanded (Priya).

Draft action items (to refine in meeting)
- AI-001: Marcus to provide perf dashboard link + flamegraphs for canary v2 and a one-paragraph summary of risk by EOD 2026-04-20. (owner: Marcus Liu, due: 2026-04-20)
- AI-002: Sofia to revert metadata TTL change in staging and run 24h soak; report results in next sync. (owner: Sofia Ramirez, due: 2026-04-22)
- AI-003: Derek to prototype autoscaler smoothing change and run canary against a smaller pool; share cost delta estimate. (owner: Derek O'Neal, due: 2026-04-27)
- AI-004: Evelyn to draft rollback playbook for kernel-selection rollouts (include monitoring thresholds and preconditions). (owner: Evelyn Park, due: 2026-04-23)
- AI-005: Maya to add a console alert for high 5xx rate on model-metadata endpoints and add runbook link. (owner: Maya Singh, due: 2026-04-21)

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Need to follow up with Cost Ops about committed vs burst accounting for Dedicated (possible billing surprise). Add to next week’s agenda if unresolved.
- Consider adding an automated smoke test that validates common model-manifest queries after any metadata service change. Low friction improvement.
- For the kernel rollout: consider slower ramp but run synthetic long-context workloads to isolate fragmentation issue.

Follow-up tracking (scratchpad format)
- [ ] Marcus: dashboard + flamegraphs (AI-001)
- [ ] Sofia: staging revert + soak (AI-002)
- [ ] Derek: autoscaler prototype + cost (AI-003)
- [ ] Evelyn: rollback playbook (AI-004)
- [ ] Maya: console alert + runbook link (AI-005)

Links / quick refs:
- Confluence: Serving Runtime - Perf Notes (CONFLUENCE-RT-1034)
- Jira: RT-2145 (kernel selection rollout)
- GH: PR 812 (kernel scheduler tweaks)

Meeting artifacts to attach after meeting:
- Finalized action-item checklist with owners and closed dates.
- Small postmortem if we decide to roll back canary and it causes a regression.

-- end of prep notes --

Personal quick log (post-meeting) - placeholder for meeting minutes / copy in here after sync.
